CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Continue the negotiating track and signal a willingness to expand our purchase commitments (we have already agreed to buy soybeans) to lock in a deal that removes the threat of the List 3 tariff hike from 10% to 25%. Do not escalate, but hold firm on core structural red lines (forced technology transfer, industrial subsidies) and keep the Huawei/Meng matter separate from the trade settlement so we do not trade away sovereignty over a national champion.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is genuinely high but not existential. US tariffs now cover ~$250B of our goods (25% on $50B, 10% on $200B), and the pain is visible in the real economy: February exports plunged ~21% y/y, the worst in three years (CNN), the official manufacturing PMI contracted to 49.4 in December (first contraction in over two years, Reuters), and growth has slowed to its lowest since the 2008 crisis. The Huawei/Meng criminal charges (Jan 28 DOJ indictment) add firm-level targeting of a flagship 5G champion, pushing this toward the upper end. But the threat is capped below existential for three PIT reasons: the US has twice postponed the March 1 List 3 hike (Feb 24), Lighthizer says a deal on forced tech transfer and subsidies is 'very close' (Politico), and a Mar-a-Lago summit between Trump and Xi is being floated for late March. The US has clear incentive to settle ahead of 2020, which is leverage for us. Because escalation would deepen the export hit and a near-term settlement is achievable, the right stance is to hold the negotiating posture rather than confront — forward progress and purchase commitments are the cheapest route to easing the tariff overhang that is actively damaging our exporters.
key_factors: US tariffs on ~$250B of Chinese goods, including potential hike of $200B tier from 10% to 25%
Feb 2019 exports fell ~21% y/y (worst in 3 years); Dec 2018 PMI contracted to 49.4 (first in 2+ yrs)
Growth slowed to lowest since 2008 crisis; global demand cooling
Huawei/Meng criminal charges = firm-level targeting of 5G national champion
De-escalation momentum: March 1 hike postponed twice; Lighthizer says deal 'very close'; possible late-March Trump-Xi summit
China's leverage lies in being a major US buyer (soybean purchases already agreed)

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
Trump tweets that talks have made substantial progress and further delays the scheduled List 3 hike from 10% to 25%.
US DOJ unseals fraud and sanctions-related charges against Huawei and Meng.
Chinese exports plunged 21% in February from a year earlier... worst monthly performance since February 2016.
Official PMI fell to 49.4 in December, below the 50-point level that separates growth from contraction.
Lighthizer told Congress a deal with China to address forced technology transfer and subsidies is very close.
